statement: Whenever the function returns a result r: let a trio be a 3-element subset T of {1,...,n} such that for every two distinct u,v in T the unordered pair {u,v} occurs among the entries of edges, and for such T let d(T) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(edges) for which exactly one of edges[i][0], edges[i][1] belongs to T. If at least one trio exists, then 0 <= r and r = min { d(T) : T is a trio }. If no trio exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 400. edges is a list with len(edges) >= 1. For every i with 0 <= i < len(edges), edges[i] is a list of length 2 whose entries satisfy 1 <= edges[i][0] <= n, 1 <= edges[i][1] <= n, and edges[i][0] != edges[i][1]. For every 0 <= i < j < len(edges), the unordered pair {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} is different from {edges[j][0], edges[j][1]} (no repeated undirected edge).
